chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, or someone else, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed Zahr, then divorced: He (peace be upon him) said: The expiation is dropped from him if he divorces before he resumes sexual intercourse. It was said: What if he reverts to her? He (peace be upon him) said: If he divorced her specifically to drop the expiation from him, then he reverted to her, the expiation remains obligatory upon him always when he resumes sexual intercourse. And if he divorced her and he did not intend anything from that, then there is no harm if he reverts to her, and there is no expiation upon him.

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: The expiation or penalty required to be paid for a specific religious violation or act.
key_terms.رَاجَعَهَا: He reverted to her (in marriage) after a revocable divorce.
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zahr: A specific form of divorce in Islamic jurisprudence where a man likens his wife's back to his mother's back, incurring an expiation.

ai.seo_question: Does a man still owe the Zahr expiation if he divorces his wife after performing Zahr?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the conditions under which the expiation (Kaffarah) of Zahr is waived or retained, emphasizing the role of intention (niyyah) in Islamic jurisprudence. It distinguishes between a divorce specifically intended to nullify the expiation, which remains binding upon resumption of intercourse, and a general divorce where the expiation is lifted. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the interplay between legal formality and internal intent in marital obligations.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, or someone else, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Musa Bin Akeyl Al Numeyri, from one of our companions,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who did Zahaar, then divorced’. Heasws said: ‘The expiation is dropped off from him when he divorces before he repeats the copulation’. It was said, ‘Supposing he reverts to her?’ Heasws said: ‘If it was such, rather he divorced her in order for the dropping off of the expiation from him, then he reverted back to her. So the expiation is necessitated for him, ever, whenever he repeats the copulation; and if it was that he divorced her and he did not intend anything from that, so there is no problem if he reverts back to her, and there is no expiation upon him’.
en.sarwar: 28. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar or others from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah, from Musa ibn ‘Ukayl al-Numayriy, from certain persons of our people who has said the following:

“About the case of a man who expresses the statement of al-Zihar about his wife then divorces her, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Expiation does not apply to his case when he divorces before going to bed with her.’ It was then asked, ‘What happens if he goes back to her?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has divorced her to escape from expiation, then goes back to her, expiation is obligatory for whenever he goes to bed with her, but if he divorced without such intention then it is not unlawful to go back to her and expiation is not due on him.’”
